tasks.title: Consolidate Geofabrik extraction while preserving world-provider workflows
tasks.notes: OWNER DECISION AND IMPLEMENTATION REQUEST 2026-11-21: consolidate extraction in shared tool code, with a small world-local wrapper supplying regional configuration and deliberate overrides. Implement in an agent on a dedicated worktree. Capture and preserve Southampton's current CLI options, output filenames, combined GeoJSON and evidence-manifest registration; the current shared extractor is not a drop-in replacement. Move useful portable capabilities into shared code with regional settings supplied as configuration, and keep standard queries in one place. Every GDAL extraction must explicitly supply OSM_CONFIG_FILE, honour deliberate local schema overrides and fall back to the shared schema. Replace the world duplicate only after compatibility is covered; preserve owner edits. Meaningful temporary-fixture/subprocess-double checks must cover furniture/schema arguments, both entry points, legacy options and outputs, manifest registration and preservation of previous good outputs on failure. Tool tests must use synthetic providers, never import the live world's implementation. A separate small change belongs in the world repository for its wrapper. No live block writes, downloads or remote writes are part of this implementation request. Original report: the world extractor omitted OSM_CONFIG_FILE and GDAL's default schema lacked the amenity column used by furniture queries, blocking prepare. A local patch selected world downloads/osmconf.ini or TOOL_ROOT/config/osmconf.ini; inspect the current file because that historical patch may now be committed. Original prepare manifest hints for prepared-53--42, prepared-54--42, 52,-42 and 52,-43 were not run; do not retroactively register those as part of this refactor.

tasks.title: Trial: railway run with real rails in a study area (owner picks the stretch)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world and the stretch, and says whether it may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md sections 5 and 6. Owner idea 2026-11-10: real Minecraft rails for long runs of railway, with land height and direction hacking. This is a spike: the deliverable is findings plus a throwaway prototype, not a production builder. Stretch: at least 300 blocks with a curve and a cutting or embankment. Steps: (1) get the railway lines for the area (railway is not in CELL_EXTRACT_LAYERS today; state where they come from, for example a one-off extract from the world's OSM provider) and snap the centreline to a rail-legal path (long cardinal runs, 90-degree corners, diagonals as staircases); (2) take a lidar ground profile along it, smooth and clamp to a gentle gradient (find the real-world figure from a source and cite it), level the corridor with cut or fill and grass side slopes; (3) lay ballast and rails, with one ascending rail only where a step is needed; (4) apply under the site lock with a structure backup and look in game with the owner. First version leaves out bridges, tunnels, road crossings, fences, stations and signals; note where each would be needed. The prototype lives in the scratchpad, or on a task/* branch only if the owner wants to keep it. Game rules to confirm on the current client: rail needs a solid block below, slopes only on straight cardinal runs at 1 block per block, curves flat, diagonals as staircases. Deliver findings in docs/plans/railway.md: what looked right and wrong, blocks changed outside the corridor, minutes and session tokens used (method stated), and a recommendation with the follow-up implementation tasks to file from the findings. Scratch effects and any snags go to the named world's repo; standing up a new world is separate world work. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and table rows; the owner's in-game verdict on whether the run reads as a railway and the corridor looks natural is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Trial: rule-built typology buildings versus per-building specs (owner picks terrace, estate and shop parade)
tasks.notes: NEEDS USER INPUT: the owner names the world and three study streets, and says whether they may be rebuilt. Plan: docs/plans/vibe-at-scale.md sections 2 and 6. Today houses use scripts/house_build.py (already a rule-based footprint builder with a small spec) and non-house buildings use a full hand-written spec in site/builds/<name>.json built by feature_build.py. Question: how much of a real district can rules cover well, using footprint, lidar height, OSM tags (building, building:levels, roof:shape) and a small per-district choice of palette and roof form. This is a spike. The prototype generates minimal specs for the existing builders (house_build and feature_build); it does not add a third builder. Baseline is house_build with a minimal spec versus a full feature_build spec for the same buildings. Study streets: a terrace, a semi-detached or detached estate street, a shop parade. Build about 20 buildings per street with the prototype and compare with the current path, noting minutes and session tokens per building (method stated) and what the player sees from the street. Pitched roofs use pitched_roof_states as it is today. Deliver findings in docs/plans/typology-buildings.md: which building classes the rules cover, what still needs a designer, cost per building under each path, and a recommendation, including whether roof and facade detail (I-006) and glazing become class recipes. File implementation tasks from the findings, not before. Scratch effects and snags go to the named world's repo. Check: findings file has a Cost heading and table rows; the owner's in-game verdict on whether the rule-built streets read as the real ones is recorded in it.

tasks.title: Woodland: dense fill, mixed species, understorey and woodland floor
tasks.notes: Deliverable: inside wood polygons, fill towards the aerial canopy cover (about 80%), mixed species and heights, understorey bushes (persistent leaves at Y+1 to Y+2) and ferns, podzol/coarse_dirt/moss_block floor with grass at the edges; labelled inference, removable through the foliage and decor masks. Owner: trees need more density. Performance evidence clarified 2026-11-21 (read-only): the trial quotes 962 s for 113 trees, but 8.5 s per tree is only an average of the reported total, not a measured per-tree bottleneck. The saved farmland trees-result.json (journal_seq 1292) records 17,915 positions, writer total 2.35 s, and 40.38 s summed across recorded apply stages; planning before site_kit.apply is not included in that result. The code already batches tree writes into one cell plan. The cause of the remainder of the reported command time is not established; profile planning and full command stages before choosing an optimisation or projecting dense-woodland cost. The earlier live-planning cache-thrash/low-probe-floor problem has a landed fix in #315 (planning from saved regions); distinguish it from the still-unexplained 962 s total. Numeric runtime limit remains to be agreed. Check: wood across the river in cell 63,-45 matches the aerial density; apply time for it stays under a stated limit; owner verdict in game. Profile 2026-11-21 (read-only dry run of trees_layer on 87,-48 under cProfile, current code with #315): 85 s total. planning_inputs 52.9 s, of which neighbour_owned 36 s (cell_journal._cell_owners rebuilds ownership per cell, uncacheable because builds are excluded; about 9 million block_id calls; scales with journal history, not tree count); dry site_kit.apply 16.9 s; surface warm-up 5.6 s; plan_cell (tree placement) 5.7 s. Dry run planted 51 trees and 10,306 blocks, not the trial's 113 trees and 17,915 positions, so it is indicative only. Current planning is about a minute, so the 962 s is not explained by planning on current code: it was pre-#315 live planning or the live apply stages (MCP write and readback), which a dry run cannot show. Next: time a live apply with the existing timed_stage output; the ownership lookup is a candidate optimisation. Live apply 2026-11-21 (87,-48, after prepare --apply cleared a stale readiness validation): 77 s wall, but NOT a clean redo and NOT the 113-tree workload. The apply did not undo the earlier trees pass (the dry run simulates that undo, apply_cell does not), so 51 crowns were skipped as trunk blocked and only 3 trees (556 blocks) were planted on top. Stages: layer planning 38.6 s, identity and readiness 4.1 s, journal begin 6.1 s, writer total 12.7 s (player hop 9.3 s), flush 3.6 s, readback 0.4 s. Side effect, owner chose not to repair: the trees mask for 87,-48 now holds 556 positions instead of the 17,915 of journal #1292, so the original trees remain in the world but are outside the mask (mask-based undo or redo would only touch the 3 new trees). A real full-workload timing needs undo then apply of the trees pass, on a cell where that is acceptable. Ghost frontier finding 2026-11-21 (ground apply on 46,-46, run from prepare then ground): the apply took 984 s and 883 s of it was the 'journal follow-ups' stage (registry.ensure writing 7 frontier ghost cells, journal #1656-1668, about 126 s and 1.1 million planned blocks per cell); every other stage summed to about 100 s. Owner decision: the ghost frontier is wanted and stays; it must be completed before a timing starts, so measure applies on cells whose frontier already exists (the follow-ups stage then takes about 0 s, as on 87,-48). This does not explain the trial's 962 s: the 87,-48 trees apply (#1292) had no ghost builds after it. Still open: a full-workload trees timing needs an open-land cell with no planned features and a valid readiness check; 46,-46 is blocked by the planned houses_burgess_road feature (must land before trees/decor) and a stale validation (#232). Full-workload trees timing 2026-11-21 (46,-46 after the houses landed and a ground redo, frontier already complete so journal follow-ups took 0.003 s; existing planner, 256 crowns, 41,160 blocks, readback 0 mismatches): about 100 s of stage time. layer planning 54.2 s; registry.begin guard reads and journal write 14.0 s; surface warm-up in apply 9.8 s; readback 8.6 s; identity and readiness 3.9 s; flush 3.3 s; writer 2.6 s; backup 1.0 s. Placement is not the cost, and the trial 962 s is still unexplained (likely before #315 and #343, or a pending frontier). A runtime limit of a few minutes looks reachable; the numeric limit is still to be agreed. Dry-run cProfile of planning (inflated by the profiler): _box about 24 s, aerial tile decoding about 14 s, lidar about 7 s, neighbour_owned about 6.6 s, plan_cell about 6 s. Filed #345 for the box filter and decode caching; not filed: profiling registry.begin and the apply warm-up, and timing ground and decor. The earlier open blockers (planned house feature, stale validation) are cleared on 46,-46. Owner feedback on the existing planner, filed as issue I-055 (held until #318): too sparse versus the aerial (dense wood with a few clearings), grass floor where podzol and ground cover belong, and no species variety. Runtime limit agreed 2026-11-21: 8 minutes for a tree build; flag at 8, kill at 12 (150%), continue to the next cell in long runs, and report every 8+ minute tree build at the end of the run. The watchdog and reporting are filed as a separate task (see the task list entry Run budget for long runs). What #318 still needs: the woodland design work (diagnose why the existing cover-based fill is still sparse; species mix; understorey; podzol/moss/fern floor) and the 63,-45 check. Proving cells agreed 2026-11-21: both 63,-45 (the wood across the river; validation stale, needs prepare --apply) and 46,-46 (small wood beside the Burgess Road houses; existing planner already applied, owner snags I-055 filed against it). The check is the woodland density matching the aerial, the apply under the 8 minute budget, and the owner verdict in game, on both. Sparse-fill diagnosis 2026-11-21 (read-only, 46,-46, existing planner dry run; lidar nDSM vs planted crown discs): cover_pixels detector calls 62% of the cell cover (>=0.6), 30% firm (>=0.9), mean 0.63; lidar says only 37% of columns are 3 m or taller (43% at 2 m); planted crowns shade 47% of the cell. Only 48% of lidar-tall (>=3 m) columns have a crown (50% at >=8 m). Of the tall columns left without a crown, 59% have aerial cover under COVER_MIN 0.6 so fill_dense never considers them (owner hypothesis: obscured crowns in dense wood are missed and become gaps; supported), 25% sit at cover 0.6-0.9 and 16% at >=0.9 (thinned by the probability ramp or the FILL_SPACING 5 grid). Crowns also shade about 29% of the cell where lidar is under 3 m, so the planner both misses tall columns and plants over low ground. Only 23 crowns are lidar-detected; about 295 candidates come from the fill, 62 of 318 skipped (34 trunk blocked). Lidar alone does not give the owner density (tall columns 37% vs 47% already shaded); aerial and lidar may differ in date or in what counts as tall, so 63,-45 is the cleaner check. Proposal, not yet decided: use lidar-tall columns left bare as a second crown source and keep aerial cover only for what lidar cannot see; this is layer-changing planner work (a stretch: ask before raising model or effort). After #345 (merged f136d5e): dry run on 46,-46 still plants 256 crowns and 41,160 blocks. planning_inputs wall time 26.9 s (the earlier live layer-planning stage was 54.2 s, which also included surface warm-up). RE-SCOPED 2026-11-21: the mechanisms are split into fixture-only tasks that any runner can take: plant vocabulary (#347), woodland floor in the ground layer (#348, blocked by #347), lidar-tall second crown source (#349), species mix (#350), understorey bushes (#351); speed (#345) and run budget (#346) are separate. Layer ownership (owner, corrected 2026-11-21): ground sets the ground level at lidar terrain height (the podzol, coarse dirt and moss floor blocks, #348); trees do only trees (#349 lidar crowns, #350 species); decor does the minor non-feature, non-tree enhancements, i.e. understorey bushes, ferns, leaf litter and other plants (#351). The rough-grass trial (trial259_roughgrass_87_m48) is the source of the floor palette. #318 now keeps what needs Claude: choosing thresholds, shares and species weights against the aerial, a ground redo then trees redo on both proving cells (63,-45 and 46,-46), the 8 minute check, and the owner verdict in game. It is blocked by #348-#351. #349 and #350 both edit trees_layer.py: run them one at a time. #348 edits ground_layer.py and #351 decor_layer.py. Open for the owner: #319's rough-grass tufts and flowers are placed by the ground layer, which the ownership rule above would put in decor.

tasks.title: Plant vocabulary: teach the surface probe the 26.2 ground-cover plants
tasks.notes:
Split out of #318 on 2026-11-21 (woodland raft). Prerequisite for the woodland floor task: the surface probe and the layers must treat every plant the game offers as a plant, not as ground.

Today lib/blocks/surface_probe.py PLANTS lists only short_grass, tall_grass, fern, large_fern and some flowers. docs/plans/park-rural.md notes the Minecraft 26.2 plants that the rough-grass trial did not use because the probe would read them as ground: short_dry_grass, tall_dry_grass, leaf_litter and bush (they suit pasture and woodland floors). Scope: (1) confirm from the repo's block data (lib/blocks/block_reference.py and any generated block list) which of these and any other ground-cover plants exist in the game version in use, and record the list with its source; do not guess names; (2) add them to PLANTS and to every place that mirrors the list (ground_layer.STEM_OR_FLOWER derives from it; check foliage.REFINE_PLANTS, block_reference patterns, decor and the readback/audit code that classifies plants) so a plant over ground is probed as plant plus ground, a probe never mistakes it for the surface, and clears treat it like other plants; (3) say in the notes which plants are two-block (like tall_grass, large_fern) if any, since placement must give them the right half states.

Acceptance, synthetic only: unit tests for the probe with each new plant above grass, dirt and podzol; existing tests unchanged. No world build step, so requiresClaude is false. Not a stretch. Related: #318, the woodland floor task.

Preflight source confirmation (2026-11-21): config/minecraft-block-ids-26.2.txt is tracked and contains minecraft:short_dry_grass, minecraft:tall_dry_grass, minecraft:leaf_litter and minecraft:bush. Its provenance header identifies Mojang 26.2 client assets/minecraft/blockstates/*.json, client jar SHA256 40896ee9f1e2bec3c934daac7e93d41e9e3d9c2f8ae0ca366d52ffbfd1afa290. These four IDs are confirmed, so the worker may start. Confirm any additional ground-cover IDs against this same list and verify placement states from real blockstate data; the word tall in an ID is not evidence that it needs two halves.

tasks.title: Woodland floor blocks in the ground layer: podzol, coarse dirt and moss at terrain height
tasks.notes:
Split out of #318 on 2026-11-21; corrected the same day. Layer ownership (owner): ground sets the ground level at lidar terrain height; trees do only trees; decor does minor non-feature, non-tree enhancements such as plants and leaf litter. So the woodland floor BLOCKS live in the ground layer, and every plant on top of them (ferns, tufts, leaf litter, dry grass, bushes) lives in decor (see the decor understorey task).

Scope: extend the existing surface step in lib/layers/ground_layer.py (rough grass, #319: ROUGH_GRASS_TAGS and the ground_texture class key, seeded per cell and column, removable through the masks, counted in the report) with a woodland floor: the surface block of a column at lidar terrain height becomes a floor mix. Gate: wood = natural=wood|scrub or landuse=forest (keep #319 behaviour for meadow, pasture and lawns unchanged; scrub keeps its pasture treatment unless the config says otherwise). Starting shares are the owner-accepted values of the rough-grass trial (trial259_roughgrass_87_m48, docs/plans/park-rural.md; owner verdict Yes, use it): 30% podzol, 10% coarse_dirt, 8% moss_block, the rest keeps the ground's grass; grass only at the polygon edge (reach in columns, default 2, tunable). All shares in config/land-use-classes.json under ground_texture (schema pattern as #319), never in code. Never touch the height: terrain stays the lidar height. Skip columns that trees, decor, features or neighbours own, as the trial did. No plants in this task.

Acceptance, synthetic only: tests with a synthetic wood polygon and lawn and meadow neighbours: floor shares within tolerance of the config over a large synthetic area, same seed same result, edge reach respected, lawns and meadows identical to the #319 output, owned columns skipped, surface Y unchanged, report counts per block. No world build step, so requiresClaude is false. How it looks on 63,-45 and 46,-46 is #318. A ground change makes ground stale on built cells, so a real cell needs a ground redo after merge (never unattended); that is #318 work. Open question for the owner, not for this task: the #319 step in the ground layer also places grass tufts, tall grass and flowers, which under the ownership rule above would be decor; left as it is until the owner decides.

tasks.title: Trees: lidar-tall columns as a second crown source
tasks.notes:
Split out of #318 on 2026-11-21 from the read-only sparse-fill diagnosis on 46,-46 (recorded in #318 notes). Finding: only 48% of lidar-tall (nDSM >= 3 m) columns have a crown; 59% of the missed ones have aerial cover under COVER_MIN 0.6, so fill_dense never considers them (dark, obscured crowns in dense wood become gaps); crowns also shade about 29% of the cell where lidar is under 3 m. Lidar is the height truth, the aerial only a guide.

Scope: in lib/layers/trees_layer.py add a pure function, for example lidar_fill(ndsm, crowns, cover, ...), that returns extra crowns (dx, dz, r) for lidar-tall columns that no crown covers, and call it from planning_inputs after the detected and aerial-fill crowns and before the mapped crowns (mapped crowns still win overlaps). Parameters as named constants, not magic numbers: MIN_NDSM (start 3.0 m), spacing/tie-break, radius from local height or the existing FILL_RADII, and a rule to stop crowns being planted where lidar is low (cover alone must not add a crown on a column whose nDSM is below MIN_NDSM when lidar is available; keep today's behaviour when nDSM is missing). Deterministic for a cell (seeded like fill_dense). Keep the report counting crowns by source (detected, aerial fill, lidar fill, mapped).

Acceptance, synthetic only: tests on synthetic nDSM and cover grids: a tall blob with no crown gets crowns, a covered blob gets none, a low column with high cover gets none when nDSM is present, missing nDSM leaves current output unchanged, results deterministic, no two crowns closer than the overlap rule. No world build step in the task, so requiresClaude is false. Choosing thresholds against the aerial and 63,-45 / 46,-46, and the owner verdict, are #318. Edits trees_layer.py: run it after #345 and not in parallel with the species task (#350). This is planner logic inside one layer, not a stretch, provided the spec stays this firm.

tasks.title: Trees: species mix per crown (oak, birch, dark oak)
tasks.notes:
Split out of #318 on 2026-11-21. Owner snag (issue I-055): every tree is the same, but the aerial shows variety. Today lib/layers/trees_layer.py voxels_for turns birch trunks into oak (user, 2026-10-14: plain oak trunks) and plant_cell_canopy.tree_voxels is the only crown generator; the planner has no species notion.

Scope: add a species mix to the trees layer: each crown gets a species chosen deterministically (seeded per cell and crown position) from a weights table in config (put it with the land-use class config, keyed by class, so woods and parkland can differ), and voxels_for builds that species' crown and trunk from plant_cell_canopy (extend it if needed: crown shape, leaf block, log block, with trunk-height variance as the doc says). Starting species from docs/plans/park-rural.md: oak, birch, some dark oak. The weights (placeholder: oak 60, birch 25, dark_oak 15 inside woods; open parkland keeps today's oak-only until the owner says otherwise) are placeholders for #318 to tune against the aerial; do not present them as evidence. Keep the owner's earlier rule intact where it still applies: say in the notes how the 2026-10-14 plain-oak-trunk decision interacts (it applied to plane trees; birch trunks should read as birch in a species mix) and ask the owner via the notes, do not silently change it. Species goes into the mask and the report so a redo strips it and counts it by species.

Acceptance, synthetic only: tests that the same seed gives the same species, the observed mix over many crowns is within tolerance of the table, every species builds a valid crown (no floating leaves, trunk grounded), single-species config reproduces today's output exactly. No world build step, so requiresClaude is false. Choosing which species the aerial supports and the in-game verdict are #318. Edits trees_layer.py and plant_cell_canopy.py: run after #345 and #349, not in parallel with them.

tasks.title: Decor: woodland understorey and ground cover (bushes, ferns, leaf litter, dry grass)
tasks.notes:
Split out of #318 on 2026-11-21; moved to decor the same day. Layer ownership (owner): ground sets the ground level at lidar terrain height; trees do only trees; decor does minor non-feature, non-tree enhancements such as plants and leaf litter. So woodland understorey and ground cover are decor, not trees and not ground. The floor blocks under them are the ground-layer woodland floor task.

Owner snag (issue I-055): the woods read as parkland and the floor is plain grass; the aerial shows a closed canopy with a real understorey. Doc targets (docs/plans/park-rural.md, natural class and the rough-grass trial, owner verdict Yes, use it): low bushes of persistent leaves, about 7% of columns with 40% two blocks high; ferns about 15%; short_grass about 8%; the trial also had podzol, coarse dirt and moss floor blocks (ground task, not here).

Scope: in lib/layers/decor_layer.py (read how decor is gated first: the #319 notes say frontage.inference false blocks planting, which is why rough grass used its own key; use the same approach, a separate woodland key in config/land-use-classes.json, shares never in code) add woodland decor inside wood polygons (natural=wood|scrub, landuse=forest): (1) understorey bushes from leaf blocks (reuse plant_cell_canopy.bush_voxels), height 1 or 2; (2) ground-cover plants on the surface: fern and large_fern where they fit, short_grass, and any of leaf_litter, short_dry_grass, tall_dry_grass that the plant vocabulary task (blocked-by) confirms exist. Shares for the new plants and for leaf litter are placeholders for #318 to tune. Rules: only on a column whose block above the surface is air; never under or in a trunk or a crown's solid blocks, never on a column the trees, features or neighbours own (decor runs after trees and reads their blocks), never within the clearance of a building, path or road, never on water. Seeded per cell and column; removable through the decor mask and counted in the report per kind.

Acceptance, synthetic only: tests with a synthetic wood, crowns and trunks: share per kind within tolerance, none on trunks or crown blocks, none outside the wood polygon, none on roads or footprints, only on air above ground, deterministic, mask round-trip, woodland key off leaves decor unchanged. No world build step, so requiresClaude is false. Density, look and the owner verdict on 63,-45 and 46,-46 are #318. Edits decor_layer.py (not trees_layer.py).
